study_title: A Controlled Study of Evidence-Conditioned LLM Patch-Gating Decisions
freeze_effective_when: The named author explicitly signs every item in docs/experiments/dsa_p3_author_signoff_v0_1.md and the resulting hashes are recorded before P4 or any model output.
one_sentence_argument: In a task-disjoint controlled patch cohort, the study will estimate how cumulative, genuinely executed visible evidence changes LLM accept policy for paired hidden-failing and oracle-positive candidates, while conditioning all uncertainty statements on the frozen tasks, models, and run window.
claim_boundary: The study estimates finite-cohort decision-policy effects, not autonomous patch correctness, software safety, real-world defect prevalence, or effects for all projects and LLMs.
C0 to C3 are cumulative evidence bundles; adjacent differences are descriptive and cannot be attributed to one field.
A balanced positive/negative cohort does not estimate deployment prevalence or accepted-patch precision.
Null, negative, heterogeneous, or wide-interval results remain reportable and do not authorize redesign or rerun.

research_questions.question: For frozen hard-negative candidates, how does cumulative visible evidence at C3 rather than C0 change the probability that a fixed model response recommends automatic merge?
For frozen oracle-positive candidates, how does cumulative visible evidence at C3 rather than C0 change the probability that a fixed model response recommends automatic merge?
Through which accept, reject, and escalate transitions do C0-to-C3 changes occur, and how do those patterns vary across the three frozen model routes?

estimands.target_expectation: Expected paired finite-cohort decision effect over independent stateless response draws within the frozen task, model, provider configuration, and calendar window.

primary.name: Delta_minus
primary.formula: P(accept | C3, hard-negative) - P(accept | C0, hard-negative)
primary.direction_interpretation: Negative values mean fewer automatic-merge recommendations at C3; no direction is declared desirable without jointly reporting the positive-candidate effect.

primary.name: Delta_plus
primary.formula: P(accept | C3, oracle-positive) - P(accept | C0, oracle-positive)
primary.direction_interpretation: Positive values mean more automatic-merge recommendations at C3; no direction is declared desirable without jointly reporting the hard-negative effect and escalation/reject pathways.

task_level_construction: For each task, candidate role, model, and repeat index, compute I(decision=accept at C3) minus I(decision=accept at C0).
Average the three paired repeat contrasts within each fixed task-model block.
Average the three frozen model values with equal model weight within task.
Average the 30 task values with equal task weight for the pooled primary estimand.

secondary: paired C0-to-C3 three-by-three decision transition matrices
descriptive_only: C0-to-C1, C1-to-C2, and C2-to-C3 adjacent contrasts
always-accept, always-reject, always-escalate, and per-model C0 baselines
outcomes.baseline_equivalence: Because both candidate roles must pass all visible checks by admission, a deterministic visible-test-pass policy equals always-accept on this cohort and is reported once, not as an independent baseline.

conditional_interval.name: paired repeat-block percentile interval
conditional_interval.scope: Conditional on the 30 frozen tasks, 3 model routes, provider configurations, and run window; it does not quantify task/project/model population sampling uncertainty.
conditional_interval.resampling_unit: paired repeat index within each fixed task, candidate role, and model block
algorithm: Within every fixed task-candidate-model block, sample three repeat indices with replacement from {1,2,3}.
For every sampled index retain the paired C3 and C0 decisions and compute the accept-indicator contrast.
Average sampled contrasts within block, then equally across models within task, then equally across tasks.
Repeat independently for Delta_minus and Delta_plus using one deterministic generator stream in that order.
Use percentile endpoints 0.0125 and 0.9875 for each primary estimand.
conditional_interval.multiplicity: Bonferroni over the two primary estimands; each interval has 97.5% marginal coverage under the conditional bootstrap procedure.

stability_analyses.project_balanced: Average tasks equally within each project, then average the nine project means equally; label as reweighting, not a confidence interval.
stability_analyses.leave_one_project_out: Recompute each pooled task-macro primary effect after deleting one project at a time; report the minimum and maximum over nine deletions, not as a confidence interval.

pre_materialization: All tasks/projects in the P1 and P2 development exclusion registries remain permanently excluded.
P2 Regular primary/reserve order and transform priority are immutable.
p4_candidate_admission: Admit an oracle-positive only when the official reference fix passes all frozen visible and hidden checks in two fresh clean environments.
Admit a hard negative only when the first applicable frozen transform passes all frozen visible checks and fails at least one independent hidden oracle in both fresh environments.
Discard without reclassification when the transform is inapplicable, a visible check fails, all hidden checks pass, or environments disagree.
Before any model call, replace a discarded primary only by the next task in frozen reserve order. If reserves are exhausted before 30 complete pairs, stop the DSA study.
model_execution: Do not exclude a valid response because of its decision, confidence, rationale, model disagreement, or effect direction.
Do not impute a missing or invalid response and do not convert it to escalate.
A retry-exhausted eligible transport failure, first schema/semantic invalid, identity drift, or frozen-hash drift stops the applicable execution stage.
exclusion_and_replacement.analysis: Analyze every frozen valid response exactly once. No post-output task, candidate, model, condition, repeat, or response exclusion is allowed except a documented integrity failure that already requires stopping rather than continuing the confirmatory study.

stop_rules: P3 remains pending until explicit author scientific-responsibility sign-off and all mechanical audits pass.
P4 stops if frozen reserves cannot yield 30 complete candidate pairs without changing transform or source order.
No smoke starts until P1 through P5 and all relevant hashes pass.
Smoke stops on any invalid response, identity/fallback/hash breach, or 26-attempt hard maximum.
Full stops on any invalid response, identity/fallback/hash breach, early hidden-label access, cost/token/window breach, or 2268-attempt hard maximum.
If the frozen model is unavailable or an official ID/price changes, stop; do not substitute a model.
If complete valid full output is not frozen by 2026-08-15T23:59:59+08:00, stop without using legacy results.

no_rerun_policy.allowed_retry: At most once for transport failure, HTTP 429, or empty response, subject to stage-wide retry and attempt caps.
forbidden_reasons: high false accepts or low correct accepts
wide interval, null effect, negative effect, or non-significance
desire to change paper type, prompt, model, candidate, transform, oracle, condition, or repeat count
no_rerun_policy.after_hidden_join: No task addition, reserve use, oracle/transform change, model rerun, or cross-version pooling.
no_rerun_policy.semantic_change: Any scientific, model-visible, schema, parser, scheduling, or analysis-semantic change terminates this study version. A later version is a separate study and is not automatically authorized.

reporting_commitments: Report both primary effects together with their conditional intervals.
Report zero, negative, heterogeneous, wide-interval, and disagreement results without directional filtering.
Keep model-specific results secondary and avoid ranking claims unsupported by this design.
Describe adjacent condition changes as bundled evidence differences, never single-field causal effects.
Disclose substantive AI assistance according to the final written venue policy and retain author responsibility for every claim.
